newsitem.title: USA: NYCE's FINEX and Malaysia's MME in joint venture.
newsitem.headline: NYCE's FINEX and Malaysia's MME in joint venture.

text.p: The New York Cotton Exchange (NYCE) and the Malaysia Monetary Exchange (MME) announced Tuesday the signing of an agreement to allow the trading and clearing of selected FINEX currency futures and options on the floor of the MME.
FINEX is the financial products division of NYCE.

The move completes FINEX's strategy of offering around-the-clock trading in currency futures to match the interbank cash foreign exchange market, NYCE senior vice president for marketing and product development, Charles Minnaar, said.
Trading FINEX currency contracts on the MME would take place during the usual Asian business day.
FINEX trades during the US business day on its floor in New York and during the European trading day in its facility in Dublin, Ireland.
No date was announced for the start up of trading on MME which is based in Kuala Lumpur.
"We would like to mirror our Dublin success in the Asian region, where no futures market for local currencies now exists," Minnaar said.

"Additionally, trading FINEX currency products on the MME will complement FINEX's intention to introduce four new futures contracts against the US dollar, including the Singapore dollar, Thai baht, Indonesian rupiah and Malaysian ringgit, which are currently awaiting regulatory approval," he said.
These contracts will mark FINEX's first move into Asian currency markets.

The Malaysia Monetary Exchange, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Kuala Lumpur Commodity Exchange, offers the only ringgit interest futures contract in the world, a three-month KLIBOR contract, MME chairman Dato Syed Abdul Jabbar Shahabudin said in the joint statement.
